newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Bank rediscount rate cut boosts Zimbabwe shares.
newsitem.headline: Bank rediscount rate cut boosts Zimbabwe shares.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares continued their march ahead on Wednesday, cheered by the central Reserve Bank's announcement that it had lowered its key rediscount rate further.
The key industrial index surged 85.22 points -- a rise of 1.2 percent -- to close at 7,096.52.

"Shares are getting a new lease of life from the trend towards lower money rates. With the rediscount rate cut the cost of money is definitely coming down and that can only be good news for the stock market," one broker said.

The central Reserve Bank said on Wednesday it had -- for the second time in two months -- lowered its benchmark lending rate to financial institutions to 27 percent from 27.5 percent, citing a decline in annual inflation.

Brokers said a rise in year-on-year consumer inflation to 20.6 percent in September from 17.7 percent in August was just a hiccup due to recent private and public sector wage settlements, fuel price hikes and periodic adjustments of administered prices.

"Even if money market rates go up this month due to higher inflation in September, we believe and the Reserve Bank seems to believe that inflation is on a downward trend and we think that trend is sustainable so the prospects are looking very good for the stock market," another broker said.

On the bourse on Wednesday, agriculture investment company Chemco leapt 400 cents to 1,500 while horticultural firm Ariston at 1,300, finance house Finhold at 900, glass company PG Industries at 500, sugar producer Hippo at 850 and cement group Porthold at 1,250 all rose 50 cents.
Winery Afdis gained 25 cents to 425, steel window producer Radar climbed 20 cents to 200 and packaging firm Hunyani added 15 cents to 380.
The only losers were Natfoods, discount house DCZ and local conglomerate TA Holdings which all shed 10 cents to 650, 160 and 130 respectively.
Minings were largely unchanged with Falgold the only mover, putting on five cents to 145. The mining index edged a marginal 0.38 points up to 1,244.47.
